whatTheyArgued: From secondary descriptions of In the Blink of an Eye (read: MusicBed summary; book itself not read): Murch noticed on The Conversation that cuts lined up with Gene Hackman's blinks, and holds that a listener blinks at the moment they 'get' an idea; a cut works as a blink that punctuates ideas; a performer's blinks tie to their thought; viewers' blinks can synchronize with a well-cut film. His Rule of Six ranks emotion first, then story, rhythm, eye-trace, 2D plane, 3D space. Quoted phrase 'the cut is a blink' is credited short phrase only.

scholarship.ref: MusicBed, 'Editing Secrets from Legendary Editor Walter Murch' (read; trade summary)
scholarship.supports: blink as punctuation of ideas; cut as blink; cuts per minute parallels

scholarship.ref: Theseus (Finnish thesis repository) 'Walter Murch's The Rule of Six' (search result only, not opened)

ourUse: pacing.js: pacingGrade measures sentence-length variance and 'blink points' (a sentence at least 35% shorter than the running mean after longer ones) and treats near-zero variance as a flatline. earned-cast.js reuses the flatline as a conversation-has-gone-flat signal. output-order.js credits Murch with owning 'the rhythm of the order', while the module places claims by the material's own temporal anchors and refuses when none are stated.

bends.ours: A blink point is a short sentence after long ones; sentence variance is the 'blink'.
bends.theirs: Blinks are physiological events of the performer or viewer when a thought lands; cuts are placed to coincide. Sentence length is a proxy we invented.

bends.ours: 'A piece that never varies has no blinks - a flatline' and 'the eye rests at a sentence boundary' (compendium work).
bends.theirs: Not found in what I read; he warns against cutting that loses the audience's rhythm, not against uniform prose.

bends.ours: Only the rhythm/blink idea is implemented.
bends.theirs: Rhythm is third of six, below emotion and story; emotion is first priority.

bends.ours: output-order.js credits Murch with the rhythm of claim order and refusal without stated order.
bends.theirs: Refusing to impose order is our law; Murch's work is about cutting, not about whether source material states an order.

bends.ours: Compendium: a film is cut where the audience blinks.
bends.theirs: He cuts where he (or the actor) would blink; audience blink synchronization is an effect of good cutting, per the summary.

fix: compendium murch.work: 'Film editor who observed that cuts work like blinks: they punctuate ideas, and a performer's blinks mark where a thought lands. Our pacing module uses sentence-length variance as a rough proxy; the flatline rule and the sentence-boundary claim are ours.'
